title: BASIS: Evaluating Belief-Aware Solutions in Interactive Settings beyond Instructions
abstract: arXiv:2602.13832v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly capable of carrying out complex, long-horizon tasks, yet effective assistance requires more than faithfully executing user instructions. Users' requests reflect their current understanding of the problem, which may be incomplete, outdated, or incorrect. When this understanding diverges from the actual task state, literal instruction following can fail to accomplish the user's underlying goal. We introduce \textbf{BASIS} (\emph{\textbf{B}elief-\textbf{A}ware \textbf{S}olutions in \textbf{I}nteractive \textbf{S}ettings}), a benchmark that evaluates whether agents can infer the mental states underlying user requests, recognize belief-reality mismatches, and use this understanding to develop appropriate solutions. translated_title: BASIS：在交互场景中评估超越指令的信念感知解决方案
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体在执行复杂的长周期任务方面能力日益增强，然而有效的辅助不仅仅是忠实地执行用户指令。用户的请求反映了他们对问题的当前理解，而这种理解可能是不完整的、过时的或错误的。当这种理解与实际任务状态出现偏差时，照字面执行指令可能无法实现用户的根本目标。我们提出了 BASIS（Belief-Aware Solutions in Interactive Settings，交互场景中的信念感知解决方案），这是一个评估智能体能否推断用户请求背后心理状态、识别信念与现实之间的不匹配，并利用这种理解来制定适当解决方案的基准。BASIS 并非仅通过显式问题来评估心理状态推断，而是同时评估此类推断的实用性以及下游解决方案的质量。
tldr: 该论文提出了 BASIS 基准，用于评估大语言模型智能体能否识别用户信念与现实的偏差，并将心理状态推断转化为恰当的解决方案，而不仅限于字面执行用户指令。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces BASIS, a benchmark that evaluates whether LLM agents can recognize belief-reality mismatches underlying user requests and translate mental-state inferences into appropriate solutions beyond literal instruction following.
